meta.title: UK public sector AI guidance sources
meta.description: Candidate and incorporated sources for the AI Guidance Explorer. Merged from the original backlog and potential_external_sources.md after URL/org research.

already_incorporated.title: Artificial Intelligence Playbook for the UK Government
already_incorporated.organisation: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) / Government Digital Service (GDS)
already_incorporated.notes: Currently powers the FAQ answers and citations on the explorer. Listed again in potential_external_sources.md — treated as incorporated, not re-added as a candidate.

fields.id: Stable slug for linking and imports
fields.title: Official document or collection title
fields.type: guidance | standard | framework | code_of_practice | action_plan | regulator_guidance | hub | community | organisation
fields.why_include: Why this source matters for the explorer
fields.related_faq_themes: Existing FAQ categories it would help answer

sources.title: Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS) Hub
sources.summary: Hub for the ATRS template, completion guidance, scope/exemptions policy, and published records of algorithmic tools used in public-sector decision making.
sources.why_include: Mandatory transparency requirement referenced throughout the AI Playbook; answers questions about when and how to publish algorithmic tool records.
aliases_from_potential_list: GOV.UK - Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard + repository

sources.title: Guidance on AI and data protection
sources.summary: ICO guidance on applying UK data protection law to AI systems that process personal data, including fairness, bias, security, and Article 22 considerations.
sources.why_include: Primary regulator view for personal-data FAQs (DPIAs, lawful basis, automated decisions, fairness).

sources.title: Guidelines for secure AI system development
sources.summary: Practical security guidelines across secure design, development, deployment, and operation/maintenance of AI systems.
sources.why_include: Deepens playbook security answers (poisoning, leakage, prompt injection, secure deployment patterns).
aliases_from_potential_list: NCSC - Guidelines for Secure AI System Development and AI guidance

sources.title: Guidelines for AI procurement
sources.organisation: Government Digital Service (GDS) / historically Office for AI and DCMS/DSIT
sources.summary: Best-practice guidance for public-sector buyers on preparing, specifying, evaluating, awarding and managing AI procurements.
sources.why_include: Core source for buy-vs-build, requirements, lock-in, and ethics-in-procurement FAQs.

sources.title: AI Insights
sources.summary: Series of technical articles on implementing AI safely and effectively in the public sector. Complements the AI Playbook with deeper implementation topics the playbook deliberately defers.
sources.why_include: Playbook update notes moved build/training depth into AI Insights; high value for filling technical FAQ gaps with citable articles.

sources.title: AI Knowledge Hub
sources.organisation: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) / Incubator for AI (i.AI) / GDS ecosystem
sources.summary: Central public-sector hub to find AI tools, approaches and shared practice. Positions itself as practical adoption support and links to official guidance rather than being a comprehensive policy source.
sources.why_include: Roadmap for modern digital government points teams here; useful for collaboration/reuse FAQs and discovering further citable sources. Needs careful citation rules (practice vs policy).
sources.notes: About page states it is not a comprehensive policy source; prefer citing underlying official guidance where answers assert requirements.

sources.title: Secure by Design
sources.summary: Mandatory cross-government approach for embedding cyber security in digital delivery, including policy, 10 principles, activities and implementation guidance.
sources.why_include: Explicitly required by the AI Playbook for AI services; answers security and spend-control related FAQs with primary security policy.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence (security.gov.uk policy and guidance)
sources.organisation: Government Cyber Unit / Government AI Security Team
sources.summary: Government security landing page for AI: points to Secure by Design, the AI cyber security code of practice, the AI Playbook, NCSC guidance, and notes the Government AI Security Team / generative AI security community.
sources.why_include: Useful index for security FAQs and discovering authoritative security sources; may also yield community/process answers.

sources.title: Data and AI Ethics Framework
sources.summary: Principles and practical activities for responsible development, procurement and use of data and AI in the public sector, with an accompanying self-assessment tool.
sources.why_include: Bridges high-level ethics principles to project actions; complements ATRS and procurement guidance.

sources.title: Ethics, Transparency and Accountability Framework for Automated Decision-Making
sources.organisation: Cabinet Office / DSIT / Office for AI (as published)
sources.summary: Seven-point framework for safe, sustainable and ethical use of solely automated and AI-assisted decision-making in government, plus a risk potential assessment form.
sources.why_include: Directly answers FAQs on automated decisions, responsibility, contestability and lawful operation of ADM.

sources.title: Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI
sources.organisation: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)
sources.summary: Voluntary code setting baseline cyber security requirements across AI design, development, deployment, maintenance and end of life; intended to inform emerging standards including ETSI work.
sources.why_include: Complements NCSC guidelines with a lifecycle code of practice useful for supplier and assurance questions.
related_urls: https://www.etsi.org/ (ETSI TS 104 223 — emerging standard informed by this code; confirm exact public URL before citing)
aliases_from_potential_list: DSIT AI Cyber Security Code of Practice / ETSI TS 104 223
sources.notes: Treat ETSI TS 104 223 as related standards work, not a substitute citation, until a stable public text/URL is verified.

sources.title: Introduction to AI assurance
sources.organisation: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) – Responsible Technology Adoption Unit
sources.summary: Accessible introduction to AI assurance concepts, techniques (impact assessment, audit, testing) and how to embed assurance in organisational practice.
sources.why_include: Supports FAQs on quality assurance, monitoring, evidence of fitness-for-purpose and governance boards.

sources.title: Service Standard
sources.summary: Mandatory standard for government services. The AI Playbook states that if you develop a service you must use the Service Standard.
sources.why_include: Foundational delivery requirement for AI services that are public-facing or meet service criteria; backs FAQ on Service Standard applicability.

sources.title: Service Manual
sources.summary: How-to guidance for meeting the Service Standard, including team setup, user research, security and privacy practices relevant to AI-enabled services.
sources.why_include: Playbook repeatedly points here for team setup and user research for AI; good supporting citations for delivery FAQs.

sources.title: Technology Code of Practice
sources.summary: Cross-government criteria for designing, building and buying technology; used in spend control and referenced by the AI Playbook for lifecycle understanding.
sources.why_include: Supports FAQs on spend controls, secure technology choices and meeting wider digital standards alongside AI-specific guidance.

sources.title: Creating practical guidance for responsible AI adoption (Roadmap for modern digital government)
sources.summary: Roadmap initiative page describing GDS work on responsible AI adoption guidance, progress (Playbook, Knowledge Hub, ethics framework, advisory panel) and next steps.
sources.why_include: Useful orientation for what central guidance exists and where GDS is heading; less suited as a primary citation for normative requirements.
aliases_from_potential_list: Roadmap for Modern Digital Government - AI adoption guidance

sources.title: AI Opportunities Action Plan
sources.organisation: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)
sources.summary: Government roadmap and response on accelerating beneficial AI adoption, including scan/pilot/scale approaches and smarter public-sector procurement.
sources.why_include: Strategic context for why government is adopting AI and how procurement and scaling may change; useful for leadership FAQs.

sources.title: Responsibly buying AI: a guide for councils in England
sources.organisation: Local Government Association (LGA), with LOTI, EHRC and ICO
sources.summary: Role-based prompts for English councils to embed Public Sector Equality Duty and data protection into AI commissioning, procurement and contract management.
sources.why_include: Extends coverage beyond central government to local public sector buyers; strong equality + DP angle.

sources.title: LGA Artificial Intelligence Hub and AI Network
sources.summary: LGA hub for council AI resources, plus peer AI Network (and practitioners network) for risks, rewards and readiness discussions.
sources.why_include: Discovery and collaboration channel for local government; cite published guides (e.g. responsibly buying AI) rather than private network discussions.

sources.title: NHS AI knowledge repository
sources.summary: NHS repository and community resources for responsible AI adoption in health and care, including the AI Ambassador Network.
sources.why_include: Sector-specific guidance for health FAQs; may conflict with or specialise central-government general advice — flag scope carefully.

sources.title: Justice AI Unit
sources.summary: MoJ Justice AI Unit site describing responsible AI embedding across justice services using a scan/pilot/scale model.
sources.why_include: Departmental practice and case context; verify which pages are citable guidance vs programme marketing before FAQ use.

sources.title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Centre (DAIC)
sources.summary: MoD centre that champions, enables and innovates AI across UK Defence.
sources.why_include: Likely limited public normative guidance; keep on watch for published defence AI policy/guidance suitable for citation.
sources.notes: Status watch: organisation presence confirmed; insufficient public guidance pages identified for FAQ citation yet.

sources.title: Government Analysis Function AI Hub
sources.summary: Single entry point for analysts to approved AI-related guidance, learning materials and standards aligned to the Analysis Function strategy.
sources.why_include: Profession-specific layer on top of cross-government AI guidance; good for analyst-oriented FAQs and discovering approved resources.

sources.title: Incubator for Artificial Intelligence (i.AI)
sources.organisation: Government Digital Service / DSIT (i.AI merged into GDS Jan 2025)
sources.summary: i.AI pioneers transformative AI applications for public good; public site also surfaces the AI Knowledge Hub. Organisational pages on GOV.UK note merger into GDS.
sources.why_include: Context and product/case discovery; prefer citing Knowledge Hub content or published guidance over org homepage alone.

sources.title: AI Security Institute (formerly AI Safety Institute)
sources.organisation: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)
sources.summary: DSIT institute focused on understanding and reducing risks from advanced AI. GOV.UK notes the rename from AI Safety Institute to AI Security Institute.
sources.why_include: Important for frontier-model safety context; less directly actionable for typical departmental adoption FAQs unless citing specific evaluation/guidance publications.
sources.notes: Cite specific published reports/guidance, not the org homepage. Confirm current public brand URL if aisi.gov.uk supersedes GOV.UK org page.

sources.title: Automation and AI Community of Practice (Wales)
sources.organisation: Digital Public Services Wales / Welsh Government
audience: Welsh public sector AI / automation practitioners
sources.summary: Monthly community of practice for people implementing automation and AI across the Welsh public sector, facilitated via Digital Public Services Wales.
sources.why_include: Devolved collaboration channel; useful for Wales-scoped FAQs and discovering Wales-specific standards/guidance. Not itself a normative guidance document.
aliases_from_potential_list: Automation and AI Community of Practice (Wales)

sources.title: GDS Responsible AI Advisory Panel
audience: GDS responsible data and AI team
sources.summary: Advisory panel convened to advise on responsible AI use across government; referenced from the Roadmap for modern digital government AI adoption page.
sources.why_include: Watch for published advice or outputs that become citable; panel itself is not end-user guidance.
sources.notes: Verify page contents and any published outputs before elevating beyond watch.
